solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: High-flier finally trading in gold to cut deal

indicators.note: to cut means this cluster splits the word for deal in two

parts.note: to deal in goods is to sell them

indicators.note: in puts the letter from trading inside the symbol for gold

parts.note: AU is the chemical symbol for gold

indicators.note: finally says to take only the closing letter of trading

explanation.surface: A high-flying financier closes a gold-trading deal at the last moment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'High-flier' suggests a City banker, which suits the trading and gold. 'finally' gives G, which goes 'in' AU to make AGU, and that cluster is put 'to cut' SELL, giving SE-AGU-LL.
explanation.definitionFit: A gull soars over the coast, so a bird is literally something that flies high.

clue.text: Sarcastic old model ruined party?

indicators.note: ruined means the letters are wrecked and rebuilt in a new order

explanation.surface: A cutting former model wrecked the celebration.
explanation.walkthrough: 'party' looks like a social gathering, but it is a political one; the question mark flags that the answer is plural members.
explanation.definitionFit: Members of a centre-left political group together make up a political organisation.

clue.text: Sterility of clot injected with unlimited enzyme

indicators.note: injected with says the trimmed enzyme goes inside the word for clot

parts.note: a clot is British slang for a fool, an ass

indicators.note: unlimited means without its outer limits, so the first and last letters go

parts.note: pepsin is a digestive enzyme in the stomach

explanation.surface: A medical note: a blood clot was injected with an enzyme for sterility.
explanation.walkthrough: 'clot' looks like a blood clot, but in British slang a clot is a fool. Pepsin is the stomach enzyme that 'unlimited' trims.
explanation.definitionFit: Asepsis is the absence of germs, the germ-free condition of surgical instruments.

clue.text: Released single

definitions.meaning: let loose, as a horse freed from its cart
not married, since getting hitched is getting wed

explanation.definitionFit: Unfastening a horse from a cart lets it go; being unwed in slang is the reverse of getting hitched.

clue.text: Dwelt, as it happens, with daughter

parts.note: a live broadcast goes out as it happens

explanation.surface: Someone stayed on with their daughter, as it happens.
explanation.walkthrough: 'as it happens' reads as a throwaway phrase but means LIVE, as in live television.
explanation.definitionFit: To have resided somewhere is to have made a home and stayed there.

clue.text: Death came back, area wiped out by a single plague

definitions.note: used here as a noun: an endemic is a disease that is always present in a region

parts.note: death is the end of life

indicators.note: wiped out by says one letter is removed and the next item takes its place
back says the word came is read from right to left

parts.note: a single thing is one, the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: Death returned and a whole district was wiped out by one plague.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' turns CAME into EMAC before 'wiped out by' makes the swap. 'plague' is a noun: an endemic is a disease.
explanation.definitionFit: An endemic is a disease permanently established among a population, a constant scourge rather than an epidemic.

clue.text: Gourmet's timeless photo following European article

definitions.note: read as gourmet is, so an adjective: being a gourmet

indicators.note: following puts the trimmed photo after the letter for European
timeless means the T, for time, is removed

parts.note: a photo is a picture
an is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A food lover's classic snapshot taken after a European newspaper article.
explanation.walkthrough: Read 'Gourmet's' as 'Gourmet is', giving an adjective. 'timeless' removes T from PICTURE.
explanation.definitionFit: Epicurean describes someone devoted to refined food and drink, a connoisseur of fine eating.

clue.text: Transfer 25% of cash in transaction

indicators.note: in puts that letter inside the word for transaction

parts.note: a transaction is a deal

indicators.note: a quarter of a four-letter word is its first letter, here of cash

explanation.surface: A quarter of the cash is transferred in the deal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Transfer' looks like a verb about money, but it is a noun: a sticker.
explanation.definitionFit: A decal is a design printed to be transferred onto glass, pottery or a model.

clue.text: Fail to connect using crude jingoism that's no good

indicators.note: crude means rough, so the letters of jingoism are roughed up into a new order

explanation.surface: Crude flag-waving fails to win anyone over and does no good.
explanation.walkthrough: 'that's no' takes G away, so the rearranged letters of JINGOISM without G give the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To misjoin parts is to join them badly, so that they fail to link up properly.

clue.text: What might be best cultivated around the present time?

definitions.text: What might be best cultivated around the present time?

parts.words: What might be best cultivated around the present time?
parts.note: present time is the season of gift-giving, and the plant flowers then

explanation.walkthrough: 'present time' sounds like now, but presents are gifts: the season of giving in late December.
explanation.definitionFit: This succulent houseplant blooms in late December, so it is grown to flower in the gift season.

clue.text: Author of the 1 across spoken language, only half finished

indicators.note: spoken says we want the letters that sound like the language's name

parts.note: Czech is the language of the Czech Republic

indicators.note: only half says to keep just the first two of the four letters

parts.note: something finished is over

explanation.surface: A writer is described by a foreign tongue, left half done.
explanation.walkthrough: 1 across is SEAGULL, Chekhov's play The Seagull. 'spoken' makes the language sound like CHEKH; 'only half' keeps OV of OVER.
explanation.definitionFit: Anton Chekhov, the Russian dramatist, wrote the play The Seagull, first staged in 1896.

clue.text: One contributing to cutting, ironic works about head of state

indicators.note: about says the rearranged letters go round the letter from state
works means the letters of ironic are worked into a new order
head of picks the leading letter of state

explanation.surface: Satirical writings take aim at a head of state, adding to the political cutting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'works' rearranges IRONIC; 'head of' gives S from state, which the rearranged letters wrap 'about'.
explanation.definitionFit: Front teeth bite and slice food, so each one does its share of the cutting.

clue.text: Plus fours finally donned by a clique

indicators.note: donned by means the letter is worn inside A SET, like a garment

parts.note: a clique is a set, a closed social group

indicators.note: finally says to take only the closing letter of fours

explanation.surface: A smart set all wearing plus fours, the baggy golfing trousers.
explanation.walkthrough: Plus fours are baggy knee-length trousers once worn for golf. 'finally' gives S, which goes inside A SET.
explanation.definitionFit: A plus is an advantage or benefit, and so is something valuable you have going for you.

clue.text: Mainly question ladies and gents about new and old money

indicators.note: mainly means most of the word, so drop its final letter

parts.note: to question a claim is to doubt it

indicators.note: about says the toilets go round the letter for new

parts.note: the Ladies and the Gents are British public toilets, loos

explanation.surface: Someone queries where the public toilets are, and asks about new versus old coins.
explanation.walkthrough: The Ladies and the Gents are British names for public toilets. 'and' simply joins the two halves.
explanation.definitionFit: Spanish gold coins of the treasure-fleet era are a classic example of currency no longer in use.

clue.text: Free record mostly difficult, say, to turn

parts.note: a disc is a gramophone record

indicators.note: mostly means most of the word, so the last letter goes

parts.note: difficult means hard

indicators.note: to turn says the abbreviation is read backwards

parts.note: say means for example, abbreviated eg

explanation.surface: Releasing a record proves rather tricky, so to speak, to turn round.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mostly' trims HARD to HAR; 'to turn' makes EG into GE.
explanation.definitionFit: To discharge a prisoner or patient is to release them, letting them go.

clue.text: Possibly flat surface in new unopened screen

indicators.note: in says the word for surface goes inside the rearranged letters
new means the remaining letters are made afresh in a fresh order
unopened means the opening letter of screen is removed

parts.note: a side is a surface, as a side of a cube

explanation.surface: A flat surface sits inside a new screen that is still unopened.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unopened' takes S off SCREEN; 'new' rearranges CREEN to RENCE, and SIDE goes 'in' it.
explanation.definitionFit: A flat is one example of a home, a place where somebody lives.

clue.text: Material essential to Sudden Impact

indicators.note: essential to says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A costume note: some fabric is crucial to the Clint Eastwood film Sudden Impact.
explanation.definitionFit: Denim is a hard-wearing twill cotton cloth, the fabric of jeans.

clue.text: Contentious society girl presently dining in Paris?

parts.note: a deb, short for debutante, is a society girl
the French a table means at the table, eating

explanation.surface: A debutante, sitting down to dinner in Paris, is controversial.
explanation.walkthrough: A table is the French call to dinner, meaning at table, which is how 'presently dining' gets there.
explanation.definitionFit: Something contentious is open to argument, a matter people may dispute.

clue.text: Beware of reported laid explosives

indicators.note: reported means we want a word that sounds like the one for beware of

parts.note: to mind the step is to beware of it

explanation.surface: A warning that explosives have been reported in the area.
explanation.definitionFit: Laying mines in ground or sea leaves that area booby-trapped with explosive charges.

clue.text: Babushka eager for fabric

parts.note: babushka is Russian for grandmother, a nan
someone eager is keen

explanation.surface: A Russian grandmother is keen to get some cloth.
explanation.definitionFit: Nankeen is a yellowish cotton cloth, originally made in Nanjing.

clue.text: Bring nuts buried by pigs for a lark or two?

indicators.note: buried by says the scrambled letters sit inside the word for pigs

parts.note: in British slang a pig of a job is a sod, an awful thing; sods

indicators.note: nuts means crazy, so the letters of bring are scrambled

explanation.surface: Bring some nuts, which the pigs root about and bury, for a bit of fun.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a lark or two' sounds like fun, but it is birds: skylarks. 'nuts' scrambles BRING to NGBIR, 'buried by' SODS.
explanation.definitionFit: Larks are singing birds, so a couple of them would be a pair of examples of the type.

clue.text: Resume method following break

indicators.note: following puts the word for method after the word for break

parts.note: a break is a rest
an art is a skill or method, as in the art of persuasion

explanation.surface: Pick up the technique again after an interval.
explanation.definitionFit: To resume an activity is to begin it again after a pause.

clue.text: Company contained, not getting one over

indicators.note: not getting says the letter for one is dropped

parts.note: something contained is included
one is I in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: A firm restrained itself and didn't get a single one over on its rivals.
explanation.walkthrough: 'over' sits at the end looking like part of 'getting one over', but it is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: When a meeting or match has finished it is said to be over, ended and done.

clue.text: Secured position in Oxford?

parts.note: an Oxford is a lace-up shoe, held fast when its laces are tied

explanation.walkthrough: 'Oxford' looks like the university, and 'secured position' like a place there, but an Oxford is a style of lace-up shoe.
explanation.definitionFit: The shoe is fastened by tying its strings, which is what it means to have it done up.

clue.text: Was about to season highly and cook

indicators.note: about says the word for was is turned round

parts.note: to have been is to have lived

explanation.surface: Someone was about to make a spicy dish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Was about to' reads like a phrase, but 'about' reverses LIVED and 'to' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Devilled kidneys or eggs are cooked with hot spices such as mustard and cayenne.

clue.text: Noble Italian ignoring prisoner's former account

indicators.note: ignoring says the letters for the prisoner are left out

parts.note: a contessa is an Italian countess
a con is a convict, a prisoner

explanation.surface: An Italian aristocrat disregards a convict's old bank account.
explanation.walkthrough: TESSA, the Tax Exempt Special Savings Account, was a British savings scheme of 1991 to 1999.
explanation.definitionFit: The scheme was a type of tax-free savings plan, since replaced by the ISA, so it is a defunct account.

clue.text: Chap against pursuing a place in France

parts.note: Len is a man's name, any chap
con means against, as in pros and cons

explanation.surface: A man argues against following someone to a French town.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pursuing a' means coming after A, so A goes first even though the clue prints it later.
explanation.definitionFit: Alençon is a town in Normandy, famous for its lace.

clue.text: Animated tirade on origins of violence inside borstals

indicators.note: on means the tirade comes after those letters in the across entry
origins of says to take the opening letter of each of the next three words

parts.note: a tirade is a rant

explanation.surface: A furious speech about how violence begins in borstals, Britain's old youth prisons.
explanation.walkthrough: A borstal was a British detention centre for young offenders.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone vibrant is lively and full of energy, as animated people are.

clue.text: Indefinitely adjourned by English following inside manoeuvring

indicators.note: following says the letter for English comes after the rearranged letters
manoeuvring means moving the letters of inside around

explanation.surface: A meeting is postponed after some backroom politicking by the English.
explanation.definitionFit: The Latin phrase, literally without a day, describes a hearing put off with no date set to resume.

clue.text: Classical father arranged authentic backing

indicators.note: backing says the two words together are read from right to left

parts.note: something arranged is set
authentic means real

explanation.surface: An old-fashioned dad sets things up with genuine support.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backing' turns both words round together, not each separately. 'Classical father' points to Greek myth rather than any old dad.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth Laertes was the father of Odysseus, so a father from classical legend.
